properties.natural_language: A block received for state transition processing must have a valid parent hash referencing an existing block in the chain.
The block header gas limit must be within 1/1024 of the parent block's gas limit (GAS_LIMIT_ADJUSTMENT_FACTOR constraint).
The block header base fee must match the value computed from the EIP-1559 formula using the parent block's gas usage and target.
In post-PoS blocks, the ommers hash must always equal EMPTY_OMMER_HASH; no uncle blocks are permitted.
After block body execution, the computed state trie root must exactly match the state_root claimed in the block header.
After block body execution, the computed transaction trie root must exactly match the transactions_root in the block header.
After block body execution, the computed receipt trie root must exactly match the receipts_root in the block header.
After block body execution, the cumulative gas used by all transactions must equal the gas_used value in the block header.
A block that passes all header and body verification checks must transition to STATE-BLOCK-APPLIED; any verification failure must result in STATE-INVALID-BLOCK.
After creating the block environment, it must contain the correct coinbase address, gas limit, block number, timestamp, and base fee from the block header.
A transaction's gas must not exceed the remaining block gas available for processing.
For blob transactions, the cumulative blob gas must not exceed MAX_BLOB_GAS_PER_BLOCK (1,179,648).
The ECDSA signature must produce a valid sender address via secp256k1_recover; invalid signatures must cause transaction rejection.
The transaction's max_priority_fee_per_gas must not exceed max_fee_per_gas, and max_fee_per_gas must be >= the block's base_fee_per_gas.
For blob transactions, all versioned hashes must use KZG version prefix (0x01) and the list must be non-empty.
The transaction nonce must exactly equal the sender account's current nonce; mismatches cause rejection.
The sender must have sufficient balance to cover gas × max_fee_per_gas + value + blob_gas_fee.
The sender account must have no code (be an EOA) or have valid EIP-7702 delegation code.
After a validated transaction begins processing, the sender's nonce must be incremented by exactly 1 before EVM execution.
Before EVM execution, gas × effective_gas_price + blob_gas_fee must be deducted from the sender's balance.
The gas refund must be computed as min(gas_used_before_refund / 5, refund_counter), and must not exceed 20% of gas consumed.
After refund calculation, the effective gas used must be at least the EIP-7623 calldata floor cost: max(gas_after_refund, calldata_floor_cost).
The sum of gas refunded to sender + gas paid to miner + gas burned (base fee portion) must equal the total gas allocated to the transaction.
The miner (coinbase) must receive exactly (effective_gas_price - base_fee) × gas_used as priority fee payment.
The base fee calculation must follow EIP-1559: if parent gas used > target, base fee increases; if below target, it decreases; change is bounded by 1/8 of parent base fee.
The effective gas price must equal min(max_priority_fee_per_gas, max_fee_per_gas - base_fee_per_gas) + base_fee_per_gas.
The blob gas price must be computed from excess_blob_gas using the exponential formula: fake_exponential(MIN_BLOB_BASE_FEE, excess_blob_gas, BLOB_BASE_FEE_UPDATE_FRACTION).
The blob data fee for a transaction must equal total_blob_gas × blob_gas_price.
The gas limit change between parent and child block must not exceed parent_gas_limit / GAS_LIMIT_ADJUSTMENT_FACTOR (1024).
The parent gas target must always equal parent_gas_limit / ELASTICITY_MULTIPLIER (2).
The BEACON_ROOTS_ADDRESS contract (0x000F3df6D732807Ef1319fB7B8bB8522d0Beac02) must have deployed code before the system call is executed.
After successful beacon roots system call, the parent beacon block root must be stored in the beacon roots contract ring buffer.
After successful history storage system call, the parent block hash must be stored in the history storage contract.
System transactions must be executed with SYSTEM_TRANSACTION_GAS (30,000,000) gas and originate from SYSTEM_ADDRESS (0xfff...ffe); if the target contract has no code, the block is invalid.
After transaction processing, deposit requests must be correctly extracted from transaction logs.
The collected requests must be ordered by ascending request type: deposits first, then withdrawals, then consolidations.
Each beacon chain withdrawal must credit the recipient account by exactly withdrawal_amount × 10^9 (Gwei to Wei conversion).
Valid delegation code for sender validation must follow the EIP-7702 format with a proper authorization chain; accounts with non-delegation code must be rejected as senders.
The rolling 255-block window for block hash lookups must maintain exactly 255 most recent block hashes; requests for hashes beyond the window must return empty.
The secp256k1_recover function must be deterministic: given the same (hash, v, r, s) inputs, it must always produce the same public key output.
A valid ECDSA signature can only be produced by the entity holding the corresponding private key; forged signatures must be computationally infeasible.
Raw transaction bytes received for decoding must begin with either a valid type prefix (0x01, 0x02, 0x03, 0x04) or an RLP list marker (>= 0xc0) for legacy transactions.
Transaction bytes with first byte < 0xc0 and not in {0x01, 0x02, 0x03, 0x04} must be rejected as invalid transaction types.
After decoding, a legacy transaction must contain exactly the fields: nonce, gas_price, gas, to, value, data, v, r, s.
After decoding a typed transaction, the type byte must be stripped before RLP decoding the remaining payload.
A transaction's gas must be >= max(intrinsic_cost, EIP-7623_floor_cost) to pass validation.
A transaction's nonce must be strictly less than 2^64 - 1 per EIP-2681; nonce overflow causes rejection.
For contract creation transactions, the init code length must not exceed MAX_INIT_CODE_SIZE.
The EIP-7623 calldata floor cost must be computed as (total_tokens × FLOOR_CALLDATA_COST) + TX_BASE_COST, where tokens = zero_bytes + non_zero_bytes × 4.
The signature R component must satisfy 0 < r < SECP256K1N; values outside this range must be rejected.
The signature S component must satisfy 0 < s <= SECP256K1N / 2 (low-s requirement to prevent signature malleability).
After signature recovery, the sender address must be derived as the rightmost 20 bytes of keccak256(recovered_public_key).
Legacy transactions with v in {27, 28} must use pre-EIP155 signing hash (without chain_id); legacy transactions with chain_id in v must use EIP-155 hash format.
Typed transactions (types 0x01-0x04) must use their type-specific signing hash format with the type prefix included.
The intrinsic gas cost must include TX_BASE_COST (21000) plus calldata cost (4 gas per non-zero byte, 0 per zero byte).
Contract creation transactions must add TX_CREATE_COST (32000) plus init code size cost to intrinsic gas.
Access list gas cost must be computed as 2400 gas per address plus 1900 gas per storage slot.
For SetCodeTransactions (EIP-7702), authorization list cost must be added per authorization entry.
A received SignedInclusionList must be from a validator whose index is a member of the inclusion list committee for the specified slot.
The inclusion_list_committee_root in the received inclusion list must match the Merkle root computed from the actual committee for the slot.
The BLS signature on the inclusion list must be valid using DOMAIN_INCLUSION_LIST_COMMITTEE domain and the validator's public key.
The inclusion list committee must consist of exactly INCLUSION_LIST_COMMITTEE_SIZE (16) validators, deterministically selected using the epoch seed with DOMAIN_INCLUSION_LIST_COMMITTEE.
After a block producer checks inclusion lists, if all forced transactions are included, the block must be IL-compliant and prioritized by fork choice.
A block missing forced inclusion list transactions must be deprioritized by the fork choice rule.
A block producer reviewing collected inclusion lists must have received them from the gossip network before block construction.
Any valid inclusion list from any committee member creates a forced inclusion obligation; the minimum quorum for enforcement is determined by the fork-choice rule.
During jump destination analysis, PUSH data bytes (following PUSH1-PUSH32 opcodes) must never be identified as valid JUMPDEST locations, even if their byte value is 0x5B.
Only bytecode positions containing the JUMPDEST opcode (0x5B) that are not within PUSH data may be added to the valid_jump_destinations set.
After jump destination analysis completes, the valid_jump_destinations set must contain every JUMPDEST position in the bytecode and no other positions.
A message call must load and analyze the target contract's bytecode for valid jump destinations before beginning opcode execution.
A JUMP or JUMPI instruction must target a position in the valid_jump_destinations set; jumps to positions not in the set must cause execution reversion.
The valid_jump_destinations set must be computed once per code execution context and remain immutable for the duration of that call frame.

During static jump destination analysis, unknown opcodes must be treated as single-byte instructions and skipped without error; during execution, undefined opcodes must raise an InvalidOpcode exception.
When an EIP PR changes the status field, all lint rules must be enforced on the entire document, including untouched lines.
When an EIP PR does not change the status field, lint rules must only be enforced on lines modified by the PR.
EIP-7199 is a meta-governance EIP with no impact on Ethereum protocol runtime behavior; it only governs CI/linting processes.
Bytecode submitted for deployment starting with 0xEF00 must be validated as an EOF container; bytecode not starting with 0xEF00 must be processed as legacy EVM code.
An EOF container must have version byte 0x01; version 0x00 and unknown versions must cause deployment failure.
EOF container sections must appear in the required order: type, code, [container], data, terminator; incorrect ordering must fail validation.
The EOF type section size must be divisible by 4 and must match the number of code sections; at least 1 code section with size >= 1 is required.
The total EOF container size must not exceed MAX_INITCODE_SIZE (49152 bytes); oversized containers must fail validation.
No bytes may exist outside declared sections in an EOF container; stray bytes must cause deployment failure.
Once an EOF container is validated and deployed, it is immutable and remains valid for the lifetime of the contract.
All Ethereum clients must implement identical EOF validation logic to maintain consensus; divergent validation causes consensus splits.
For EOF contracts, execution must begin at the first byte of code section 0, not at byte 0 of the container.
For legacy contracts, execution must begin at byte 0 of the bytecode.
Opcodes in the EOF reject list must cause immediate execution failure when encountered in EOF contract code.
EOF contracts must not DELEGATECALL to non-EOF (legacy) contracts; such calls must fail as if a depth-check failure occurred.
EXTCODESIZE on an EOF contract must always return 2 (length of 0xEF00); EXTCODECOPY must return at most 2 bytes from 0xEF00; EXTCODEHASH must return keccak256(0xEF00).
Deployed EOF containers must have data body matching exactly the declared data section size; the 'shorter' allowance applies only to initcode/factory scenarios.
Each EVM operation trace must contain mandatory fields: pc, op, opName, gas, stack, and depth.
For EOF container execution, trace output must include section and functionDepth fields; these fields must be absent for legacy code.
The error field in trace output must only be present when an exceptional halt occurs; it must not appear on normal operation completion.
One JSON trace line must be emitted per executed EVM operation, followed by a single summary line at transaction completion.
When an exceptional halt occurs, the error information must be captured and the STOP trace line must be suppressed.
When a contract runs out of instructions without explicit STOP, the STOP trace line must also be suppressed.
Trace consumers must accept both Number and Hex-Number formats for numeric fields interchangeably; implementations may output either format.
Tracing endpoints must have appropriate access restrictions in production environments to prevent information leakage and DoS via resource-intensive trace generation.
A received SyncCommitteeMessage must have a slot equal to the current slot within MAXIMUM_GOSSIP_CLOCK_DISPARITY tolerance.
The validator sending a SyncCommitteeMessage must be verified as a member of the correct sync committee subnet via compute_subnets_for_sync_committee().
No duplicate SyncCommitteeMessage from the same validator for the same slot on the same subnet may be accepted.
The BLS signature on a SyncCommitteeMessage over the beacon block root must be verified as valid before the message is propagated.
A received SignedContributionAndProof must have a valid slot, subcommittee_index < SYNC_COMMITTEE_SUBNET_COUNT, and non-empty aggregation bits.
The aggregator's selection proof must confirm eligibility, and the aggregator's public key must belong to the declared subcommittee.
Both the selection proof signature and the aggregate signature on a contribution must be verified as valid BLS signatures.
During fork transition, nodes must subscribe to both pre-fork and post-fork gossip topics; pre-fork topics must be unsubscribed exactly two epochs after the fork epoch.
Application-level deduplication caches must be shared between fork variants during the transition period to prevent message reprocessing.
For successfully decompressed gossip messages, the message ID must be SHA256(MESSAGE_DOMAIN_VALID_SNAPPY + topic_length + topic + decompressed_data), truncated to 20 bytes.
For failed Snappy decompression, the message ID must use MESSAGE_DOMAIN_INVALID_SNAPPY with the raw (undecompressed) data.
Valid and invalid message domain prefixes must be distinct to prevent ID collisions between valid and invalid messages for the same raw data.
After KECCAK256 execution, the 32-byte Keccak-256 hash of the specified memory region must be pushed onto the EVM stack.
KECCAK256 requires at least 2 elements on the stack (memory offset and size) and space for 1 result push; stack underflow must halt execution.
KECCAK256 gas cost must equal GAS_KECCAK256 + (ceil(size/32) × GAS_KECCAK256_WORD) + memory_expansion_cost.
If the total KECCAK256 gas cost exceeds available gas, execution must halt with an out-of-gas error.
When size=0, KECCAK256 must return the hash of empty input (the well-known constant keccak256('')).
If the memory region requested by KECCAK256 exceeds current allocation, EVM memory must be expanded before reading data.
